title: Tar (Azerbaijani long-neck lute)
summary: The tar is a long-necked lute of Azerbaijan with a double-bowled wooden body topped by a thin skin, shaped like a figure eight. Its paired strings are plucked with a small plectrum to set out the modes of mugham, the classical art of modal singing and playing.
howToPlay: The neck carries fretted places; each lane marks the note on one string and fret.
A bead slides down the string toward its place. Pluck that note just as the bead lands.
Notes marked with a small wave are the in-between pitches of the mode, slightly off the usual steps.
Begin with the climb and return, then try the rhythmic piece in six and the rising phrase.
rules: The notes follow a mode that uses two in-between pitches between the usual steps, marked with a wave.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
The rhythmic piece is felt in six beats.
Every tune is played through twice.
heritageNote: The tar is the central instrument of mugham in Azerbaijan, where singers and players explore a mode through long, improvised sections. Makers carve the body from mulberry wood and cover it with the membrane, and the craft is passed on in workshops and music schools.
credits: Tradition: the Azerbaijani tar and mugham modes; melodies written for this game
